summary.text: A 50-year-old man with infectious arthritis of the left knee and comorbidities including diabetes, hypertension, renal insufficiency, hyperlipidemia and a history of cerebral infarction was admitted in December 2024. After pain and limited mobility in March 2022 he had arthroscopic meniscus suture surgery, was diagnosed with a left knee joint infection, and had arthroscopic debridement in June 2022. He then underwent total knee replacement with vancomycin-mixed bone cement.

Postoperatively he received enoxaparin sodium, parecoxib sodium and intravenous vancomycin 1 g. On the eighth postoperative day hemoglobin fell sharply to 44 g/L with elevated indirect bilirubin, lactate dehydrogenase and reticulocytes, negative blood cultures and positive urinary occult blood. Hemolytic anemia was suspected and an emergency blood transfusion was required.

Workup showed AB, Rh CCDee blood type, autoagglutinated red cells, positive direct antiglobulin tests with anti-IgG and anti-C3, newly positive antibody screening with possible anti-N and IgG antibodies. Vancomycin-dependent antibodies with greater specificity for the N antigen were demonstrated, platelet counts stayed normal, other causes of hemolysis were excluded, and drug-induced immune hemolytic anemia was diagnosed with Probable causality.

Vancomycin was discontinued and, under an N antigen-negative transfusion protocol, three units of red blood cells were given on the evening of the eighth postoperative day. The patient died in the early morning of the following day of cerebral infarction with shock; the effect of the transfusion and the de-challenge response could not be assessed.

article_limitations: Figure 1 values and annotations are pixel content recorded in the visual submission only; the hemoglobin 44 g/L and indirect bilirubin 131.4 μmol/L values also appear in the text and are recorded from it.
Reagent-cell antigen profiles in Tables 1 to 3 are reagent properties, not patient results, and are not recorded as patient facts.
Several discussion statements are author hypotheses (residual drug, IgM to IgG transition, causal link to cerebral infarction) and are kept as ambiguities.
Hospital admission is dated December 2024 in the case text; no exact dates are given for the surgery, transfusion or death beyond postoperative days.
No supplementary material is listed for this article.
Table 1 defines 0 as no agglutination; Tables 2 and 3 print 0 without their own legend, so their zero cells are flagged negative only where the text states no agglutination or no reactivity.
Table 3 rows using normal AB-type serum are laboratory control experiments with another person’s serum and are not recorded as patient results.
Vancomycin frequency conflicts between the abstract (every day) and the case text (every 12 h); only the frequency is quarantined as review-only.
